environment: Humpback whale mums and calves are putting on a show along the Sunshine Coast as the spring migration hits its peak
Volunteers plant thousands of seedlings in Moreton Bay's seagrass recovery push, giving dugongs and turtles a helping hand
science: Queensland researchers roll out a smarter AI tool that spots bushfire risk zones weeks before the danger season kicks in
sports: Broncos and Cowboys fans gear up for finals fever as both Queensland sides lock in NRL September action
stories.overview: Outback Queensland turns into a sea of gold and purple as spring wildflowers carpet the channel country after good winter rain

segments.title: The Open
segments.script: G'day and welcome to ParkSyde Bright Side, I'm Alex Mercer, and mate, it is a ripper of a Friday to be alive in Queensland. We've got whales, wildflowers and a bit of footy fever to get through, so settle in. I'm Jamie, and honestly Alex, today's rundown is the good stuff we live for. Spring has properly sprung and the whole state seems to be showing off a little. Too right. Grab your cuppa, we've got environment, science, weather and sport coming your way, all good news, no doom scrolling required.

segments.title: Green Desk
segments.script: Let's kick off with the environment, and it is peak whale season along our coast right now. Mumma humpbacks and their calves are being spotted rolling and breaching off the Sunshine Coast as they make their way back south. Yeah I saw the photos, absolute units cruising past like they own the joint, which fair enough, they kind of do. Meanwhile down in Moreton Bay, volunteers have been out planting seagrass seedlings to help the dugongs and turtles get a proper feed. It is such a simple thing, planting a few thousand seedlings, but it makes a massive difference to that whole ecosystem. Two great reminders that a healthy bay and a healthy coastline go hand in hand.

segments.title: Science & Tomorrow
segments.script: Onto science now, and Queensland researchers have been busy building a smarter AI tool that can flag bushfire risk zones weeks out from the danger season. It crunches vegetation and weather data to spot the trouble spots before they become actual trouble. That is genuinely brilliant, giving crews a head start instead of playing catch up when the mercury climbs. It is the kind of quiet science win that does not make huge headlines but could save homes and bushland down the track. Exactly, less drama, more prevention, which is our favourite kind of science story. Big tick from us for the boffins on that one.

segments.title: Weather
segments.script: Cheers Alex, and look, it is shaping up as a proper spring cracker across the south east. Expect plenty of sunshine through the weekend with tops around the mid to high twenties in Brisbane, cooler starts down near thirteen or fourteen so grab a jumper for the dog walk. Winds are staying light, humidity is low, so it is perfect weather for the beach, the balcony or just hanging the washing out and actually having it dry. Keep an eye out for a few king tides around the bay this week, nothing dramatic, just spring doing its thing, and hay fever sufferers, the wattle is out in force so stock up on the tissues. Back to you two.

segments.title: The Scoreboard
segments.script: Righto, sport, and finals fever is well and truly building with both the Broncos and the Cowboys locking in their September campaigns. Two Queensland sides still dancing this late in the year is nothing to sneeze at. I love finals time, the whole state gets a bit louder at the pub on game day. Fingers crossed for an all Queensland decider, though I know that is probably wishful thinking on my part. Never say never Jamie, stranger things have happened in September footy. Either way, get around your team this weekend, it is shaping up to be a cracking finals series.

segments.title: Overview & Outro
segments.script: And to finish us off today, something truly awe inspiring, out in the channel country the outback has burst into colour after that good winter rain. We are talking carpets of gold and purple wildflowers stretching to the horizon. Honestly, photos of it look like something out of a painting, it is one of nature's best kept secrets out west. If you ever get the chance to see it in person, do it, it does not happen every year. A reminder that even after a tough dry stretch, this state has a knack for bouncing back with a bit of colour and life. That is the Bright Side spirit right there. It really is. Thanks for spending your Friday with us, we will be back tomorrow with more good news from around Queensland. Look after each other out there, get outside and enjoy that sunshine. See ya tomorrow, Queensland.
